links.outcome: Output variability and reproducibility across repeated runs in multi-step agentic clinical workflows
links.effect: Small per-step variations led to substantial divergence in multi-step trajectories; variability strongly influenced by model selection and decoding temperature; instruction-following failures (unknown actions) added instability.
links.quote: We empirically evaluate VA-AAT on simulated and real-world clinical workflows, demonstrating that small per-step variations can lead to substantial divergence in multi-step trajectories.

unlisted_practices: Trajectory-level repeatability metrics linking variability to graded oversight strategies for agentic AI

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates a framework (VA-AAT) measuring trajectory-level uncertainty and repeatability metrics in multi-step clinical AI agents, evaluating its effectiveness as a diagnostic signal for deployment oversight and risk-sensitive governance.

primary.practice: repeatability and trajectory divergence monitoring for risk-informed oversight
